subject: Realtime degradation: periodic chunk-pauses from proxy causing 5xx and latency spikes
messages:
From: David Li <david.li@nexahealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime: intermittent pauses in streamed responses — urgent

Hi Camila,

We're seeing repeated pauses (2-10s) in the WebSocket token stream from Redwood across multiple sessions this morning. The client shows chunks arriving, then silence, then a burst of tokens. End users observe UI stalls and we see a correlated spike in 502/504s and increased latency in our telemetry.

Attached is a trimmed server log and a short tcpdump covering 3 incidents (nexa_stream_log_1205.txt, nexa-tcp-trace-1205.pcap). This started around 08:50 PST and has recurred every ~20–40 minutes.

Our SRE flagged it as P1 because revenue paths in the triage app are impacted. Can you confirm if Redwood is running any maintenance or if there are known routing/backpressure regressions? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
David
David Li
Platform Engineering
NexaHealth Inc
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: David Li <david.li@nexahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: intermittent pauses in streamed responses — urgent

Hi David — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts.

We're triaging now. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the affected sessions are routed through your customer proxy (you indicated platform team) or directly from clients? Also, does the client use chunked transfer over a reverse proxy (e.g., nginx/Envoy) with HTTP/1.1 or are you on native WS? The tcpdump helps but I want to be sure about the path.

Markus (cc'd) is on call to look at runtime traces; Grace is looped for exec visibility. We'll provide an initial finding within 45 mins and follow up with mitigation options (temporary config, routing, or a fallback).

- Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, David Li <david.li@nexahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: intermittent pauses in streamed responses — urgent

Folks — quick engineering triage summary (initial):

- Correlation: our telemetry shows that the affected connections share a common proxy path (IP block provided by Nexa) and exhibit bursts where the server continues to generate chunks but the client TCP window stalls for ~2–8s. After the stall, chunks arrive in quick succession which explains the UI snapback.
- Error pattern: upstream 502/504s are hitting when the reverse proxy times out on an inactive stream; Redwood's backend is returning continuation frames but the proxy is closing the socket.
- Possible root causes: proxy-level backpressure (buffering + aggressive idle timeouts), mismatched chunk flush behavior from client/proxy, or intermittent TLS re-negotiation/handshake stalls at the proxy layer.

Immediate mitigations we can apply from our side (low friction):
1) Enable explicit heartbeat frames and reduce max chunk buffer size on the runtime to force more frequent flushes (potentially reduces aggregation but improves perceived latency).
2) Temporarily route NexaHealth traffic to a less-loaded Dedicated pool with a tuned keepalive profile while we debug proxy behavior.
3) Provide a small client-side recommended patch (send smaller application-level frames / disable Nagle) as a quick patch for Nexa.

I attached a short playbook (playbook-backpressure-v1.pdf) with the steps and rollback criteria. We'll try mitigation (1) in a canary and watch for reduction in pause frequency — target within 2 hours.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: David Li <david.li@nexahealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 11:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: intermittent pauses in streamed responses — urgent

Thanks Markus.

Confirmed: the traffic is routed through our edge proxy cluster (Envoy-based, managed by our platform team). We saw the same pattern on direct client tests and via the proxy, but the proxy idle timeout is set to 15s and we see closures around that window sometimes. We'll try a client patch to disable Nagle — I'll coordinate a quick test with our FE team.

Please proceed with the canary you suggested. We appreciate the quick turnaround.

-David

If the canary doesn't show clear improvement we should be prepared to offer a short-term credit and schedule an exec call tomorrow with Nexa leadership.

- Grace
